family_title_en: Complete the word with the correct digraph

stages.ix_title: Complete the word with the correct digraph: ch, sh, th, ph, wh

prompt.en: Which two letters complete the word?

what_to_do.en: Tap the two letters that fit.

stages.choice_rule: Four different pairs from ch, sh, th, ph, and wh. Exactly one pair completes the word the stem means, and the answer index changes from item to item. The stem begins with First or End, and that is where the pair sits. Never offer a full word, one letter, tch, or a made-up sound.

gold_items.stem: First of a very big boat.
First of a round bike part.
End of an animal in a lake.
First of an image on a desk.
First of a number before four.
First of food kids eat from a bag.
First of a question <NAME> may ask about an area.

roots: Offer four different pairs from ch, sh, th, ph, and wh. Exactly one pair completes the word the stem means.
A wrong pair must not complete another real word that fits the same stem.
Tier 1 wrong pairs should not build any common word a child knows for that clue.
Tier 3 includes one near-miss pair that builds a different real word, such as sh for ship when the clue means chip, or th for there when the clue means where.
Choices are only those two-letter pairs. Never a full word, never one letter, and never tch, shr, or thr.
No stem word may contain the consecutive letters ch, sh, th, ph, or wh. Do not use the, that, this, they, she, with, what, when, or school.
If a stem word begins with c, s, t, p, or w, do not offer ch, sh, th, ph, or wh as a wrong choice for that same first letter.
Use whole words from the roots list about home, food, pets, play, family, or weather. No brand names and no real personal names. Use <NAME> for a person.

Begin the stem with First or End so the child knows where the two letters sit. ph and wh only start words here, as in photo, phone, wheel, and where. Do not use tch words such as catch, match, or watch.

tier_rules.1: Four to six words. A very common word such as ship, wheel, or chick. The clue fits only one word. Wrong pairs do not build another real word.
tier_rules.2: Six to eight words. Use the end of a word, as in fish, or a two-syllable word such as photo. A clear number word such as three is fine. Wrong pairs do not fit the clue.
tier_rules.3: A longer clue with one near-miss pair that spells a different real word. Chip traps ship. A question about an area traps there. The stem still fits only one pair.
